If 19 July 2000 was a Wednesday, then what would be the day of the week on 15 June 2012?
solution:
We will count the total number of days from 19 July 2000 to 15 June 2012 and calculate the number of leap years and normal years.
Years Breakdown

  • From 19 July 2000 to 19 July 2011 → 11 years

  • From 19 July 2011 to 15 June 2012 → Nearly 1 year


Leap Years [Extra Day in February]
Leap years: 2004, 2008, 2012 → 3 leap years
Normal years: 2001, 2002, 2003, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2009, 2010, 2011 → 9 normal years
Count Days from 19 July 2011 to 15 June 2012

  • From 19 July 2011 to 19 June 2012 = 11 months

  • Subtract 4 days [from 19 June to 15 June]


Days in each month

  • July 19 to December 31 → 166 days

  • January 2012 → 31 days

  • February 2012 [leap year] → 29 days

  • March 2012 → 31 days

  • April 2012 → 30 days

  • May 2012 → 31 days

  • 1 June to 15 June 2012 → 15 days


Total days from 19 July 2011 to 15 June 2012:
166+31+29+31+30+31+15=333 days166 + 31 + 29 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 15 = 333 days 333÷7=47 full weeks+4 extra days
Since 19 July 2011 was a Thursday,

  • +4 days → Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday → Friday


Thus, 15 June 2012 was a Friday.

question: In a class of 75 students, 40 students participate in Cricket, 28 students participate in Hockey, and 12 students participate in both Cricket and Hockey, whereas 19 students do not participate in any of the two sports. How many students participate only in Hockey?
solution:
In a class of 75 students.
19 students do not participate in any of the two sports.
Students who participate in any of the two sports or both the sports = 75 - 19 = 56
12 students participate in both Cricket and Hockey.
40 students participate in Cricket.
Students who participate only in Cricket = 40 - 12 = 28
28 students participate in Hockey
Students who participate only in Hockey = 28 - 12 = 16
Clearly, 16 students participate only in Hockey.
Hence, '16' is the correct answer.
